messages:
Anna: quick sync — ran a small microbench on console panel endpoints to repro the RBAC-induced latency spike. posting numbers and a proposal.
Matt: curious, which endpoints and dataset size?
Anna: panels: /dash/{id}/tiles and /dash/{id}/panel_data. workload: 50k requests, 10k unique panels, mixed authz (tenant, role, team).
Anna: baseline (authz in query-layer): p50=37ms, p95=128ms, cpu spike on query-workers.
Anna: moved authz to projection-layer (filtering after projection, with role hash in cache key): p50=42ms, p95=62ms, overall CPU lower but cache churn higher.
Qing: nice — can you share the microbench script?
Anna: gist: https://redwood.internal/gists/bench-authz-199111 (private) — main trick: simulate varied role lists, 30% cache hit.
Rahul: high-level: query-layer authz = simpler cache semantics (per-user query) but expensive because we run policy engines during planning. projection-layer = cheaper per-request planning but requires cache partitioning by authz.
Jamie: tradeoffs: increased cache key cardinality if we include role hash. that can blow memory for hot panels across many small teams.
Qing: thought: do hybrid — do fast allow-list checks in query layer (cheap opa-lite), defer full policy enforcement to projection for complex cases. cheap checks reduce tail.
Anna: rough config idea:
```
# authz config
authz.mode = "hybrid" # options: query|projection|hybrid
authz.query_fast_checks = ["tenant_equal", "team_in_list"]
cache.key = panel_id + ":" + prefix + ":" + (if fast_ok then "G" else sha(role_list))
```
Matt: pragmatic. how would we detect "fast_ok"? runtime hints from policy eval?
Qing: policy can return a boolean fast_hint when it only used simple predicates. only heavy regex/group lookups return false.
Rahul: ops concerns: if we add role-hash to cache key, eviction and mem footprint need measurement. also invalidation when team membership changes — we'll need a TTL+pubsub to nuke keys.
Anna: proposal for next 3 sprints:
- week1: instrument current authz codepaths with histograms and role-cardinality metrics (per-panel role distinct count)
- week2: implement hybrid authz toggled by config flag behind feature gate
- week3: run 2-week canary (10% traffic) with metric dashboards: p95 latency, cache hit ratio, mem usage, invalidation events
Matt: +1. add alert for cache-mem > 75% and p95 regress > 15% versus baseline.
Jamie: also add sampling traces for requests that are filtered by projection vs query so we can see cost per path.
deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled when feature-flag is set to true. will post status. :rocket:
Anna: QA note: ensure sauce tests include membership churn scenario (simulate removing user from team -> panels should reflect).
Qing: I'll prototype the fast_hint in policy infra. expecting small changes, can land behind flag.
Rahul: I'll size cache impact with synthetic role cardinality (10k, 100k distinct role combos) and post numbers to the thread.
Anna: ok. thanks all — we'll sync in the architecture sync on Friday with numbers and a proposed rollout dashboard. :thumbsup:
